item.title: Multi-Capacity Online Assortment Optimization with Consecutive Stays under Markov Chain Choice
item.description: arXiv:2610.27661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study online assortment optimization under Markov chain choice and independent Bernoulli arrivals, with each period's request type known in advance. Each product may have multiple interchangeable physical copies, and each booking reserves consecutive service slots on a single copy. Customers choose among products, while the platform assigns purchases to feasible copies. We develop a sales-based relaxation that upper-bounds the optimal online revenue and use it to design a policy with two components: independent sampling and purchase--update coupling. We generate independent copy proposals and make a product eligible whenever at least one of its copies proposes. A general revenue-extraction bound for random candidate sets with independent product inclusions shows that optimizing over eligible products recovers at least half of each period's relaxation revenue benchmark in expectation. A purchase--update coupling reproduces the interval flows through independent virtual copy updates while preserving physical feasibility. Under general Markov chain choice, the policy uses a random gate to make the coupling feasible: it offers the selected assortment with probability \(1-1/e\) and the empty assortment otherwise. No gate is needed under multinomial logit (MNL) choice. The resulting policies achieve approximation ratios of \((1-1/e)/2\) and \(1/2\), respectively, relative to the optimal nonanticipative online policy, independently of product capacities. In the single-copy MNL setting, our policy improves the guarantee of \citet{huwu2026} from \(0.271\) to \(1/2\) under the same arrival convention. The \(1/2\) static extraction factor and the \(1-1/e\) uniform scalar-gate factor are separately sharp, and the \(1/2\) MNL guarantee is tight for the proposed policy.
item.dc:creator: Hongbin Zhang, Yanzhi Li, Woonghee Tim Huh

item.title: When Weak Submodularity Meets Matroids: How Does Standard Greedy Behave?
item.description: arXiv:2610.26967v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weakly submodular maximization finds numerous applications in machine learning, data mining and statistics. In particular, under a cardinality constraint, the standard greedy algorithm is known to attain the tight $(1-e^{-\gamma})$-approximation guarantee, where $\gamma$ denotes the submodularity ratio. However, when considering general matroid constraints, \emph{how well standard greedy can perform} has remained a longstanding open question. In this paper, we resolve this question by studying the worst-case approximation guarantee $R_{\mathrm{gr}}(\gamma,r)$ of standard forward greedy, where $r$ is the rank of matroid. Specifically, our first contribution is the following refined lower bound \begin{equation*} R_{\gr}(\gamma,r)\ge \max\left\{ \frac{\gamma}{r}, \frac{\gamma^2} {B_\gamma+\sqrt{\gamma(r-1)}}, \frac{\gamma^{r+1}} {2-\gamma+\gamma^{r+1}}, \frac{\gamma^2} {14\left(B_\gamma+\sqrt{\gamma(1-\gamma)(r-1)}\right)} \right\}, \end{equation*} where $B_\gamma\triangleq2-\gamma+\gamma^2$. This lower bound not only strictly improves upon the previous guarantee of $0.4\gamma^2/(1+\sqrt{\gamma r})$, but also can recover the classical $1/2$-approximation guarantee at $\gamma=1$. Subsequently, a corresponding upper bound is established for $R_{\mathrm{gr}}(\gamma,r)$, namely, \begin{equation}\label{eq_upper_abstract} R_{\gr}(\gamma,r) \le\min\left\{\frac{1}{2},20\max\left\{\frac{\gamma}{r}, \frac{\gamma^2}{B_\gamma+ \sqrt{\gamma(1-\gamma)(r-1)}}\right\}\right\}. \end{equation} For every fixed $\gamma\in(0,1)$, this Eq.\eqref{eq_upper_abstract} effectively sharpens the recent $O_\gamma(1/\log(n-1))$ upper bound to $O_\gamma(r^{-1/2})$, where $n$ is the size of ground set. Putting all these results together, we eventually can obtain \[R_{\gr}(\gamma,r) = \Theta\!\left( \max\left\{\frac{\gamma}{r}, \frac{\gamma^2} {1+\sqrt{\gamma(1-\gamma)r}}\right\} \right).\]
item.dc:creator: Qixin Zhang, Shi Fu, Shengminjie Chen, Chao Qian, Dacheng Tao

item.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture and improved bounds for bipanchromatic colorings
item.description: arXiv:2610.27133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the bipanchromatic number $\chi_B$, introduced by Lalou et al. (Discrete Appl. Math. 391 (2026), 511-522) as the maximum number of colors in a panchromatic hypergraph coloring where every color appears at least twice. They show that merging uniquely occurring colors in a maximum panchromatic coloring gives the lower bound $\beta=\chi_P-\lceil\alpha/2\rceil \leq \chi_B$, where $\chi_P$ is the panchromatic number and $\alpha$ is the minimum number of such colors among maximum panchromatic colorings. They conjectured that $\chi_B=\beta$ and subsequently disproved it (arXiv:2610.08042). We identify the smallest counterexample, with six vertices and three hyperedges, both minimum possible. We show that the ratio bound $\chi_B/\beta<2$ is asymptotically sharp and prove minimality results for the order and hyperedge count. For $3\le\alpha<\chi_P$ we show that every integer from $\beta$ to $\chi_P-1$ occurs as $\chi_B$ while $\chi_P$ and $\alpha$ are held fixed. Furthermore, we discover that the values $|V|,\chi_P,\alpha$ directly decide whether the conjectured equality holds except when $\alpha=4$, where a matching reduction resolves the ambiguity. We derive the optimal universal lower bound $L$ depending only on $|V|,\chi_P,\alpha$ in the nontrivial regime $0<2\alpha<|V|$. Finally, we prove $\chi_B/L\le5/4$ and $\chi_B/L\le6/5+1/(5L)$, with $5/4$ sharp and $6/5$ asymptotically sharp as $L\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Novakovi\'c, Du\v{s}ko Joji\'c

item.title: ARRIVAL in cube-root subexponential time
item.description: arXiv:2610.28241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the ARRIVAL problem, a token travels through a switch digraph: at every vertex, it leaves along one of two out-arcs, and the two are used alternately. The question is which of two terminals the token reaches first. ARRIVAL lies in $\mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}$, but no polynomial-time algorithm is known.The fastest known algorithms turn some vertices into terminals and search for consistent guesses of the numbers of tokens that these vertices send out. The first, due to G\"artner et al. [ICALP 2021], searches all vertices at once with an algorithm for fixed points of monotone maps, and the second, due to Haslebacher [ICALP 2025], searches one vertex at a time by binary search. Both search for a fixed point of the same map, which returns how many tokens arrive at the guessed vertices. We guess the vertices in blocks of $k$, between these two extremes, which needs a search in $k$ dimensions with few evaluations of this map. To do so, we build on the connection between ARRIVAL and $\ell_1$-contractions established in the second of these works. We search with $\ell_1$-centerpoints of the remaining guesses, which are guaranteed to exist by Haslebacher et al. [FOCS 2025], and which we approximate deterministically. In order to prove our results, we show how to find the least fixed points of maps from $\{0, \ldots, N\}^k$ to itself that have unit increments. For ARRIVAL on $n$-vertex switch digraphs, this gives run time $2^{\mathcal{O}(n^{1/3} \cdot \log^{2/3} n)}$, improving the previous time bound of $n^{\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n})}$. We work with the more general \garrival problem, with many tokens and several terminals, and solve it in the same time when there are at most $2^n$ tokens.
item.dc:creator: Ebrahim Ghorbani, Raul Lopes, Matthias Mnich

item.title: Isolation of non-triangle cycles in graphs
item.description: arXiv:2510.08361v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a set $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs, we call a copy of a graph in $\mathcal{F}$ an $\mathcal{F}$-graph. The $\mathcal{F}$-isolation number of a graph $G$, denoted by $\iota(G, \mathcal{F})$, is the size of a smallest set $D$ of vertices of $G$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ intersects the vertex sets of the $\mathcal{F}$-graphs contained by $G$ (equivalently, $G-N[D]$ contains no $\mathcal{F}$-graph). Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the set of cycles, and let $\mathcal{C}'$ be the set of non-triangle cycles (that is, cycles of length at least $4$). Let $G$ be a connected graph having exactly $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The first author proved that $\iota(G,\mathcal{C}) \leq n/4$ if $G$ is not a triangle. Bartolo and the authors determined a set $\mathcal{E}_4$ of nine graphs such that $\iota(G,\{C_4\}) \leq n/5$ if $G$ is not an $\mathcal{E}_4$-graph. Chen and Cui recently strengthened this result by proving that $\iota(G, \mathcal{C}') \leq n/5$ if $G$ is not an $\mathcal{E}_4$-graph. This had been proved by Zhang and Wu for the case where $G$ contains no triangle. Various authors proved that $\iota(G,\mathcal{C}) \leq (m+1)/5$ if $G$ is not a triangle. We prove that $\iota(G,\mathcal{C}') \leq (m+1)/6$ if $G$ is not a $4$-cycle. Zhang and Wu established this for the case where $G$ contains no triangle. Our result yields the inequality $\iota(G,\{C_4\}) \leq (m+1)/6$ of Wei, Zhang and Zhao. These bounds are attained by infinitely many (non-isomorphic) graphs. The proof of our inequality hinges on also determining the graphs attaining the bound.
item.dc:creator: Peter Borg, Dayle Scicluna

item.title: There is no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph
item.description: arXiv:2609.37978v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A graph is $K_3$-irregular if its vertices belong to pairwise distinct numbers of triangles. We prove that no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists, settling the last unresolved case. Following the initial discovery of such graphs for regularities $r \in \{10,11,12\}$ (Stevanovi\'c et al., 2024), our previous work (Hak et al., 2025) showed that no such graphs exist for $r \le 7$, provided the first example for $r=9$, and proved that any $8$-regular candidate must have between $17$ and $22$ vertices. We exclude these possible orders for $r=8$ by combining careful analysis of triangle degrees with integer linear programming techniques. Meanwhile, a recent construction (Zhang, 2026) established that regular $K_3$-irregular graphs do exist for all $r \ge 9$. Together with our results, this establishes that an $r$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists if and only if $r\geq 9$.
item.dc:creator: Artem Hak, Sergiy Kozerenko, Andrii Serdiuk

item.title: Metric Dimension is NP-complete on Graphs of Treewidth Two
item.description: arXiv:2610.21133v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The metric dimension of a connected graph is the least number of vertices whose distance vectors distinguish all vertices. We show that deciding whether the metric dimension of a graph is at most a given integer is NP-complete on graphs of treewidth at most two, and even on two-connected two-terminal series-parallel graphs of pathwidth at most five. As the problem is polynomial on trees, the graphs of treewidth one, this settles the treewidth threshold of its hardness, which was known to lie between two and twenty-four. The reduction is from satisfiability of formulas in which every literal occurs at most twice. To such a formula with $n$ clauses and $r$ variables it associates a two-terminal series-parallel graph $G_\varphi$ with $O((n+r)^2)$ vertices and pathwidth at most five, whose metric dimension is $2(n+r)+7$ if the formula is satisfiable and $2(n+r)+8$ otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Benoit
